family.tagline: Three people, one Companion Core, and a house on a knoll above the water.
family.story: Minjung keeps the household running from the dining table, and Jiho builds apps in the little study. Yuna, eight, reads in her room upstairs. One Companion Core sits in the living room.

companion.name: Poppy
companion.job: Drafts replies to the piano teacher and the swimming club from Minjung’s short notes.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Minjung reads and sends every message.

companion.name: Linnet
companion.job: Drafts changelogs and commit notes from Jiho’s rough fix notes.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Jiho reads every word before it is used.

popup.title: Jiho and Yuna carry it in
popup.body: A courier leaves the parcel on the stone stoop. Jiho and Yuna carry it in to the credenza in the living room.

popup.title: Yuna lays out the contents
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Yuna lays the pieces out in a row.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Jiho plugs in the cable and Minjung presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Minjung joins from her phone
popup.body: On her phone, Minjung opens the Wi-Fi settings and joins the Core’s own network. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Minjung picks the first agent
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Minjung picks Hermes. The family adds Forgejo and BookStack, and then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Poppy says hello
popup.body: Minjung sends her first message to the agent she named Poppy. Poppy answers from the Core, which sits in the living room.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: minjung
say.text: Hello, Minjung. I am Poppy. Where shall we begin?

beats.capability: stream your own music collection from your Core

popup.title: Jiho queues the weekend playlist
popup.body: Saturday morning light crosses the grand piano as Jiho chooses the weekend playlist from the sofa. Navidrome plays the family’s own music files from the Core.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains at the DNS level

popup.title: Jiho points the router at Pi-hole
popup.body: From the loveseat, Jiho sets the router to ask Pi-hole for web addresses. Pi-hole on the Core blocks ad and tracker domains for devices that use it for DNS.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes and chores

popup.title: Minjung adds rice to the list
popup.body: Tuesday afternoon, the rice runs low. Minjung marks it at the breakfast bar in Grocy, which keeps the pantry stock and shopping list on the Core.

beats.capability: assign and track household chores, with NFC tag completion

popup.title: Yuna ticks off the fruit bowl
popup.body: Setting out the fruit bowl is Yuna’s Wednesday job. She holds the family phone to a tag on the fridge. The Donetick rota on the Core marks it done.

beats.capability: write a wiki or a set of manuals in books, chapters and pages

popup.title: Minjung starts with the pump
popup.body: For the guests, the water shutoff and pool pump restart go on page one. Minjung writes the manual in BookStack, which keeps it on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Poppy drafts the reply
popup.body: The piano teacher asks to move Thursday’s lesson. Poppy drafts the reply on the Core’s local model. Minjung reads it, changes one word and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: minjung
say.text: Here is a draft reply. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Minjung scans the mooring letter
popup.body: A mooring fee letter and a swimming form get scanned at the dining table. Paperless-ngx reads them on the Core, and Minjung finds the letter later by a word.

beats.capability: back up your files with encryption before they leave your Core

popup.title: Jiho backs up the manual
popup.body: Jiho sets a weekly backup of Minjung’s manual and scans. Duplicati encrypts them before they leave the Core, and the copy lands on a disk plugged into it.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: Jiho checks the terrace camera
popup.body: A cushion keeps ending up in the upper pool, so Jiho checks the terrace camera. Frigate recorded an otter, and the clip stays on the Core.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Minjung sets the pump timer
popup.body: Friday morning, Minjung plugs the pool pump into a smart plug. Home Assistant on the Core runs the timer, and Home Assistant itself needs no cloud account.

beats.capability: host your own git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: One bug left before lunch
popup.body: One tide table bug is left, so Jiho pushes the fix before lunch. Forgejo keeps the code and issues on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Linnet drafts the changelog
popup.body: Jiho types his fix notes to Linnet in his browser. Linnet drafts the changelog on the Core’s local model, and Jiho reads it before he pastes it into Forgejo himself.

say.speaker: jiho
say.text: Here is the changelog. Please read it before you paste it.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: Jiho hunts a late tide table
popup.body: One tide table comes out an hour late. Jiho reruns the sums in JupyterLab, then asks a model on the Core, through Open WebUI, what he missed.

beats.capability: turn text into natural speech on your own Core

popup.title: Yuna hears her otter story
popup.body: Yuna types three lines about the otter on the terrace. Kokoro on the Core speaks them back, and she fixes the funniest sentence.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Yuna writes the card first
popup.body: For her grandmother’s birthday, Yuna writes a card in Korean, then checks it in LibreTranslate. Its language models were downloaded once, and the Core does the translating.

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech

popup.title: Yuna has the page read aloud
popup.body: Beside the low bookshelf, Yuna opens the family’s own ebooks in Koodo Reader and has it read the page aloud. The library lives on the Core.

popup.title: One Core on the knoll
popup.body: A manual, a camera, code and an otter story read aloud, on one Companion Core on the knoll.

closing.body: Your house manual, camera clips, code and read-aloud stories can sit on a Companion Core. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: Walk order: ftue and living (Core on the credenza), kitchen and dining on the entry level, the garden terrace and pools, then upstairs to the study and Yuna's room, then the street. Garden sits before the stairs on purpose.

No TV in this house: living-music is the couch media beat (Navidrome). The grand piano is named only as a piano. The Living Room has no laptop or screen, so the Pi-hole beat is a router setting from the loveseat.
The Study has a desk and a laptop only; no monitor or screen is named. The Kids Room has a bookshelf and no desk: Yuna's beats anchor the bookshelf or the room.
Both companions are Hermes. Memory is not connected, so Companion Memory is never named. Poppy and Linnet only draft; Minjung sends, Jiho pastes.
Pi-hole covers only the devices that use it for DNS; the beat says so and is not parental control. Frigate: the camera is the family's own, over their own terrace.
The LibreTranslate beat carries downloaded once. Donetick is told without its Telegram or Pushover notifications. Home Assistant needs a network smart plug for the pump; no Zigbee stick is implied.
Duplicati names a local disk as the destination. Paperless-ngx is scans only. Kokoro speaks only the text typed into it; it answers no questions and no voice or language is named.
Jiho's tide table app is a personal project: no employer code is implied.
